timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How does DLP actually know what's sensitive?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It uses sensitive info types — patterns like credit card numbers, SSNs, and custom formats you define.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: EDM lets you hash and index your actual sensitive data. DLP checks content against the index with high precision and low false positives.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Endpoints, Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams. All covered by unified policies in Microsoft Purview.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What happens when DLP detects something?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Policy tips educate the user. Admins get incident reports. You can block, warn, or just log the activity.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Tune your rules, use trainable classifiers, and review incident reports. It's an iterative process.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. If Copilot tries to surface sensitive data in a response, DLP blocks it. Even AI needs guardrails.
